result: {"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the bottom body line (stroke 2) and laid it from the nose back toward the tail crossing. It branches off the nose, so the start feeds both body lines, and it showed dark (connected to the start) all the way to the crossing. In the last minutes I took on the fish's fork notch, which was the last open area. I laid the upper join from the fork into the pale pair in the middle of the notch. I was laying the lower join when time ran out, so I can't say it was finished. Execution: I picked one piece of work, the bottom line, and kept at it quietly until it was done. I coordinated the joins with Leo, who came forward along the bottom from the tail. When the notch became the remaining gap, I moved onto it. I asked the others to keep off the notch so we wouldn't bump each other. When the supply of dominoes ran short, I asked teammates to lift pale strays so I could keep building. Collaboration: I stayed in step with the table. I gave a clear status update at the midpoint so everyone knew what was live and what was open. I took Priya's description of the two open notch ends and acted on it. I accepted the spare dominoes the others sent and let them handle the upper tail and crossing. Leadership: I backed Priya's fish plan right away and committed to my stroke. I summed up where the build stood and where the open spot was, and in the final stretch I took the last critical gap so the others could clear strays and fix jams around it. Overall, my share is a real but partial part of a four-person build. The start, top line and tails were laid by teammates.", "my_share_percent": 25}
